proposal.summary: Retain existing fetch-recovery guidance; refine discovery deduplication and semantic completeness checks with two targeted updates.

edits.title: Inspect results and resolve aliases before recording discoveries
edits.content: Empty discovery placeholders caused stalled_search issues even when later calls recorded entities for the same queries. After each search, inspect its results and record actual newly discovered entities once; for search_many, do this separately for each query in input order. Do not emit [] before inspection or assume a later record erases an earlier event. Compare entity identities, not just exact name strings: punctuation variants, omitted initials, and contextually identified surnames can refer to already known entities. Maintain evidence-supported aliases without merging ambiguous names. Use [] honestly when no new entities were found, including verification searches that supply new field evidence. Do not invent discoveries or count known aliases as new entities to suppress stall warnings.

edits.title: Recover missing or incomplete fields from rendered pages
edits.content: When a model-rendered fetch returns usable but incomplete text, identify the specific missing or incomplete fields before fetching again. Request concise factual summaries with brief supporting excerpts rather than full-page reproduction. Test a revised focus on one page and inspect its evidence before expanding. Preserve each response with its URL and focus so later responses do not overwrite earlier support. Before new retrieval, review saved evidence for fields an extraction omitted. Keep unstated fields unresolved and use alternative sources instead of inferring facts from birthplace, institutional location, or ambiguous collective descriptions. Validate quotes against an individual saved response, then separately check that they support the correct entity, field, time, and full requested scope. A nonempty value and matching quote do not establish completeness: flag summaries or excerpts when exact wording is required, and verify attribution of shared statements. Track these semantic gaps alongside empty cells; do not insert editorial gap notes into factual values. Retrieve only the unresolved evidence, repair affected cells, and repeat both membership and semantic checks. Match the task's evidence contract: rendered-text membership does not authenticate a quotation against raw source text. FETCH_FAILED calls for bounded retries and source switching instead.

additional_candidates.description: Exact-string novelty checks counted name variants and surnames of known entities as new discoveries.
Semantic review recovered omitted evidence and incomplete populated fields that passed quote-membership checks.

decisions.reason: All 16 occurrences concern follow-up verification: six year-level nationality queries, three targeted affiliation/nationality queries, four person-level nationality queries, and three final audit queries. Their empty discovery records are consistent with already known entities; several searches supplied useful missing-field evidence. The existing memory explicitly permits honest empty verification discoveries. These signals do not establish repeated placeholder misuse or consistently bad memory outcomes, regardless of the passing self-check.

Reviewed all 21 failures: ten initial Nobel URLs, then LIGO, EurekAlert, Campus France, Scientific American, Le Monde, Tokyo, three Nature pages, a CV, and Leopoldina. The run tracked attempted URLs, tested a small alternative-source batch, reused saved hits, and recovered through usable alternative evidence, including another CV and an APS source. Existing fetch-recovery memory covers this behavior. Neither URL formatting nor a universal domain failure is established. Recurring backend failures alone do not justify deleting guidance that supported recovery.

The discoveries ledger labels omitted-initial variants, apostrophe variants, and later bare surnames as new_entities after the corresponding people were already discovered. The trajectory uses exact-string set membership. Final row deduplication recovered output coverage, but discovery accounting remained inflated. Extend the existing discovery memory with evidence-supported identity resolution.

Quote checks repeatedly passed while an exact-motivation field remained an excerpt; later even the empty-cell check passed with an editorial incompleteness note in that value. Semantic audits also found usable saved evidence omitted by extraction and attribution problems in shared quotations. Targeted retrieval and repair resolved these before final validation. Extend the existing recovery skill with this successful audit procedure; its empty usage/outcome history provides no basis for deletion.
